task: Replace the plain-function lxml.etree.XMLParser and lxml.etree.iterparse overrides in the code-executor runtime guard (filesystem_policy.py) with hardened, class-compatible subclasses that keep all XML protections and parser tracking, plus regression tests.

key_reasoning.reason: The closest existing pattern is the current hardened factory functions and the parse wrappers that consult the tracked-parser set. They define the protections but not class-compatible subclassing: a user subclass that sets its own kwargs (the FontTools setdefault shim) must still be forced to the safe values and tracked. The approach is proven by a prototype in the real executor image, which puts the base at M. It is bumped to L because the change sits in XXE/entity-expansion hardening, which is security-sensitive. The existing subprocess XXE and billion-laughs tests give a template for error-path assertions, so the edge-case auto-bump does not apply.

One component changes: the lxml block of the runtime prelude template inside install_guard. The fromstring/XML/parse wrappers stay unchanged, and all three execution paths (Jobs, shared pod, workspace script) pick up the fix from the same backend-injected prelude.

The acceptance criteria are explicit, and the fix shape is named and prototyped. Minor open points: lxml.html import breakage is extra impact not in the ticket, matplotlib/FontTools validation needs the Linux executor image because the backend venv's fontTools predates the shim, and AC 8 is a process decision rather than code.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M to L: security requirement (XML external-entity / entity-expansion hardening in the sandbox guard must remain enforced)
